title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. Pages 762–763 continue La Longue Marche. Grothendieck is building a Z-extension of G = GL(2,R)^{±1} (real 2×2 matrices of determinant ±1). He uses the 'construction 10)': G acts on the circle S_0 of rays in R^2, and G~ consists of g together with a lift of its action to the universal cover R → S_0 ≅ U, t ↦ exp(2iπt). On p.762 a lift of u is identified with a choice of argument t of u(1)/|u(1)| (formula (12)). This gives extension (13), 1→Z→GL(2,R)^{±1~}→GL(2,R)^{±1}→1, and over the neutral component its restriction (14), 1→Z→SL(2,R)~→SL(2,R)→1. The Proposition states that SL(2,R)~ is connected and homeomorphic to R^3. The purpose, made explicit on p.763, is to define GL(2,Z)~ as a preimage and present it by generators and relations, starting from the finite cyclic subgroups generated by ρ (order 6) and σ (order 4). This is the genus-1 / Teichmüller material of the Longue Marche, where SL(2,Z)~ is the braid group B_3.

This page, proof of the Proposition. The inclusion U = SO(2) ↪ SL(2,R) (15) is a homotopy equivalence. Topologically it is the inclusion U → U×R^2 (Iwasawa/polar decomposition). So it suffices to show that the preimage U~ of U in SL(2,R)~ is the universal cover R of U. For u in U, choosing a lift ũ means choosing t in R with exp(2iπt) = u(1)/|u(1)|. Since u(1) = u for a rotation, this is choosing t with exp(2iπt) = u, i.e. exactly the exponential cover. Then the cover over U×R^2 is R×R^2 = R^3: connected, simply connected, so it is the universal cover. O.K.

Cor. 1. The preimage in SL(2,R)~ of a finite cyclic subgroup of order n is ≅ Z. It has a unique generator ϖ with ϖ^n = ω0', where ω0' generates Ker(SL(2,R)~ → SL(2,R)). Proof: conjugate the subgroup into U = μ_n, whose preimage is (1/n)Z ⊂ R. This proof is carried out on p.763.

Margin. Let W be the preimage of the centre {±1} of SL(2,R). It is the centre of SL(2,R)~, infinite cyclic, generated by ω0 (the lift t = 1/2 of rotation by π), with ω0^2 = ω0'.

Cor. 2. Conjugation by an element g of determinant −1 acts on ω0' by ω0' ↦ ω0'^{-1}, and on the centre ω0^Z by ω0 ↦ ω0^{-1}. Reason: a reflection reverses the orientation of the circle of rays, so it acts by −1 on its π_1 (and sends the lift of rotation by t to the lift of rotation by −t).
errors: No mathematical error. The only gap is that 'U ↪ SL(2,R) s'identifie topologiquement à U → U×R^2' is asserted without proof; it is standard (Iwasawa KAN or polar decomposition).
In Cor. 1 'unique generator' is correct only with the normalisation ϖ^n = ω0' (rather than ω0'^{-1}), which Grothendieck does impose. Uniqueness follows from torsion-freeness of Z.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but entirely standard proof that the universal cover of SL(2,R) is R^3 with centre Z, plus routine corollaries on lifts of finite cyclic subgroups and on the inversion action of determinant −1 elements. This is preparation for the known presentation of GL(2,Z)~ / B_3; nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Cor. 1 should read roughly: 'Les images inverses dans Sl(2,R)~ d'un sous-groupe cyclique fini d'ordre n sont ≃ Z (∃! générateur ϖ de celle-ci, tel qu'on ait ϖ^n = ω0', où ω0' est le générateur de Ker(Sl(2,R)~ → Sl(2,R)))'. The 'sous-groupes discrets' and 'vs' in the machine transcription are misreadings, and the insertion is probably 'd'ordre' rather than 'd'indice' (consistent with ϖ^n).
Margin plausibly reads: 'Et W l'image inverse du centre {±1} de Sl(2,R), on trouve qu'il est engendré par un ω0 ∈ Sl(2,R)~, avec ω0^2 = ω0''. Here ω0 lies in Sl(2,R)~, not in Sl(2,R).
In Cor. 2, 'Gl(2,R)^{-1}' denotes the coset of determinant −1 matrices in Gl(2,R)^{±1}.
'quotient au-dessus de 1 par 0' is likely '(pointé au-dessus de 1 par 0 ...)', i.e. the universal cover R pointed at 0 over 1 ∈ U.
